content.title: Logan Webb takes blame after ‘all hell broke loose' in Giants' Opening Night loss
content.text: SAN FRANCISCO – Every single Giants fan at Oracle Park rose out of their seats to cheer before the first pitch of Wednesday’s game against the New York Yankees was even thrown. That is the effect of Logan Webb, who was given a standing ovation during pregame introductions on MLB Opening Night. The momentum carried over into the first inning, as Webb struck out the first two batters he faced – including Aaron Judge – before Cody Bellinger flied out to left to end the inning in a 1-2-3 punch. San Francisco’s offense failed to capitalize on continuing the momentum, and despite having a runner on first and third with one out, the game remained scoreless heading into the second inning. But momentum has a funny way of working. It can accumulate really quickly, but it also can die out within the blink of an eye if not taken advantage of. San Francisco Giants Find the latest San Francisco Giants news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Bay Area and California. Webb's third pitch of the second inning, an 85 mph changeup to Giancarlo Stanton, put the first Yankee on base. Webb would then put the next six batters he faced on base, bringing in five runs for New York. He put an end to the misery by, ironically, striking out Judge and Bellinger. The Giants would get just three hits the rest of the game, getting shut out by a final score of 7-0. The last time they were shut out on Opening Day at home was on April 3, 2007 – also a 7-0 loss – to the San Diego Padres. Webb gave up seven runs, six earned, and allowed nine hits, one walk and struck out seven over five innings. “Yeah, they just started kind of ambushing,” Webb said postgame. “I threw all the pitches I wanted to throw, not necessarily where I wanted to throw them, but yeah.” Giants manager Tony Vitello shared his perspective on how the second inning played out. "With the hit by pitch [on Jazz Chisholm Jr.], you know, it kind of played into that deal, but it wasn't really wild. You know, from my perspective, of course, you always go back and watch the video, he's attacking, and they were attacking. They got to him early in the count a few times. Seemed to have made a little bit of an adjustment to be more aggressive. But, you know, overall, he's a ground ball pitcher, and the ball got elevated a couple times. "And again, it's not like those guys were launching balls, you know, over outfielders' heads or over the fence, but they stacked their hits together. And some of that came from the bottom of the order that had success, too." The two-time MLB All-Star had allowed seven runs just twice previously in his career. He is the first Giants pitcher to allow at least six runs in a season opener since Gaylord Perry back on April 7, 1970. It should be noted that Perry finished that season second in Cy Young Award voting. A potential positive? Webb struck out Judge three times. The three-time AL MVP would strike out one more time, and Judge finished the game 0-5 after grounding out in his final at-bat. But Webb wasn’t as encouraged by his 1-on-1 battle versus Judge, given how the rest of his outing went on Wednesday. “I could care less,” he said, firmly. Webb said the conversation with him and Vitello was clear-cut when the first-year manager decided to pull Webb after the fifth. “He just told me I was done,” Webb recalled Vitello telling him. The applause Webb was welcomed with by the Oracle Park crowd was hijacked by the many Yankees fans in attendance for their star pitcher, Max Fried, who pitched 6.1 scoreless innings for New York and walked to the dugout with loud applause. Webb exited Wednesday’s game with a 10.80 ERA. He -- and everyone else around him -- knows he can do better. He has to. And while it's just Game 1 of 162, he took every ounce of blame for Wednesday's result. "I mean, it just sucks," he said. "I put our team in a position that we’re in. The first inning was great. Second inning, all hell broke loose. And that’s on me." Download and follow the Giants Talk Podcast
